item.title: Body odors may signal cancer, Alzheimer’s, and Parkinson’s through volatile compounds
item.description:
Source: Washington Post Original headline: Can odors from our bodies signal Alzheimer’s, cancer and other diseases?
Researchers are exploring how body odors, including breath and skin volatiles, may signal diseases like cancer, Alzheimer’s, and Parkinson’s. Nurses have long used smell to detect infections, while historical figures like Hippocrates linked body odor to illness. Modern studies show animals like dogs and rats can detect conditions such as cancer and tuberculosis. Scientists are developing noninvasive tests using volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in breath, urine, and sebum. For example, TOBY, a urine-based test for bladder cancer, received FDA Breakthrough Device status in 2026 and aims for commercial launch. Sebum analysis by Joy Milne and Perdita Barran identified 84% accuracy in detecting Parkinson’s. Breath tests for flu and common cold show promise, with VOCs linked to viral replication and immune responses. Challenges include variability in breath samples and contamination, but advances in machine learning and sensors may soon enable home or clinic-based diagnostics. Researchers also seek to differentiate bacterial and viral infections to guide antibiotic use, with potential applications in critical care settings.

item.title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle
Germany faces ongoing challenges in finding a permanent site for nuclear waste disposal. The country has been searching for a suitable location for nearly a decade, with only 5% of its territory under consideration. The Federal Company for Radioactive Waste Disposal (BGE) aims to identify a site by 2050, but progress remains slow. Unlike Finland, which approved a deep underground repository in 2015, Germany has yet to finalize a plan. Experts emphasize the need for geological stability, with sites requiring rock layers over 100 meters thick to ensure safety for thousands to millions of years. The BGE spokesperson, Dagmar Dehmer, highlighted Finland's success in gaining public trust through consistent government action. Current storage costs amount to €1.4 billion annually, with the final repository estimated at €14 billion. Germany's search continues amid public resistance and technical complexities, with 28,000 cubic meters of waste needing permanent storage.

item.title: Walmart and Costco Outpace Traditional Grocers in Grocery Sales
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: The latest update on the grocery wars is here, with Walmart and Costco gaining ground
Walmart and Costco are outpacing traditional grocers like Kroger and Albertsons in US grocery sales. Data from Numerator shows Costco's retail food and beverage share rose to 8.4%, up 0.5 percentage points from last year, while Walmart's share increased to 20.3% despite a 0.2 percentage point gain. Kroger's share fell to 8.2% and Albertsons' to 4.5%. Rising inflation and cost pressures are driving consumers toward value-focused retailers. Costco has maintained stable prices, but Deutsche Bank warns Walmart may face higher costs from diesel and transportation, though it remains the lower-priced option. Kroger is adopting Walmart's strategies by hiring former Walmart CEO Greg Foran to cut costs and improve efficiency, including workforce reductions and supplier renegotiations. Albertsons is adjusting employee benefits to manage healthcare costs. The shift underscores a broader trend toward value-driven competition in the grocery sector.

item.title: Vintage photos show London's 1920s landscape and century changes
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Vintage photos show what London looked like 100 years ago
Vintage photos reveal London's 1920s landscape and century-long changes. Trafalgar Square, named in 1830, retained its structure but saw fountains built in 1845. Oxford Street, now pedestrianized, had no cars in 1920. Piccadilly Circus, created in 1819, became a tourist hub. The River Thames had 35 bridges today, with traffic jams on bridges. Bicycles were common, and civil aviation grew with 10 flying clubs established in 1924, reaching 21 by 1928. The Houses of Parliament, built in 1837, stood on the Thames. King George V reigned, while Stanley Baldwin led the Conservatives. Fashion shifted to simpler styles, with flappers symbolizing 1920s women. Women gained voting rights in 1928, expanding eligibility to 15 million. Automatic telephones replaced female switchboard operators. Public pools like Chiswick Baths (1910) and dance halls, including the Hammersmith Palais, thrived. Slums persisted before 1930s clearance. The photos highlight contrasts between past and present, from urban infrastructure to social changes.

item.title: L.A. County Charter Amendment A changes labor negotiation process
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Your last-minute guide to L.A. County Charter Amendment A
L.A. County Charter Amendment A would require binding arbitration for unresolved labor disputes involving public safety workers. The measure changes the current process, where county supervisors can impose final offers on sheriff’s deputies, firefighters, lifeguards, and other employees. Under Amendment A, if negotiations reach an impasse, a three-member arbitration panel would decide. The county and union would each select one member, with the third chosen jointly or via a state list if agreement fails. Arbitrators would address wages, hours, and other terms, holding hearings and issuing a public, binding result. The amendment aims to replace the existing system where supervisors unilaterally set terms, ending the legal prohibition on strikes for public safety personnel.

item.title: Neocloud Firms Face Scrutiny as AI Bubble Fears Grow
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: These firms you've never heard of are feeding fears the AI bubble could burst
Neocloud firms like CoreWeave and Nebius, which provide computing infrastructure for AI developers, face growing scrutiny as investors question their financial stability. Analysts predict 80% of neocloud firms will cease operations by 2030, with Forrester forecasting three will be acquired due to financial strain. CoreWeave, which owes $35.1bn, relies on long-term leases with major clients like Microsoft and Meta, though lenders often prioritize customer creditworthiness over the firms' own. Recent stock declines, with CoreWeave losing a quarter of its value, reflect investor unease. Debt investors demand higher returns as interest rates rise, complicating borrowing. Some neoclouds originated in crypto mining, positioning them to capitalize on AI's 2022 boom. However, reliance on volatile AI spending plans and customer decisions, like Microsoft's reduced AI forecasts, risks their stability. Elon Musk warned over 200 neoclouds could face 'guppy-level death' due to rising costs. Despite demand for computing power outpacing supply, analysts note the sector's high financial risk. Recent setbacks include Microsoft canceling a deal with Nscale and Australia's Firmus shelving an IPO, raising concerns about the sector's future.

item.title: Daylight Saving Time Ends Tonight; Clocks Fall Back One Hour
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Daylight saving time ends tonight. Here's when to set your clocks back
Daylight saving time ends Sunday as clocks fall back one hour at 2 a.m. Nov. 1, providing an extra hour of sleep and earlier evenings. Most phones adjust automatically, but analog clocks require manual changes. The Sunshine Protection Act, a congressional bill, seeks to make daylight saving time permanent, though it faces opposition. Senator Tom Cotton has resisted the proposal, citing concerns about children commuting in darkness. Sleep experts argue standard time would better align with natural sleep cycles and reduce health risks, though some studies link permanent daylight saving to increased pedestrian accidents. States like Hawaii, Arizona, and U.S. territories do not observe the change. California voters approved ending DST in 2018, but legislative efforts have stalled. Daylight saving time will resume March 14, 2027.

item.title: Study finds colon cancer in young patients has distinct cellular traits
item.description:
Source: Washington Post Original headline: Clues emerge on why colon cancer may be harder to treat in young people
A study analyzing 189 frozen colorectal cancer tumor samples from patients aged 20 to 90 found tumors in younger patients display distinct cellular traits linked to treatment resistance and aggressive spread. Researchers observed higher stromal cell presence in younger tumors, which may shield cancer from immune cells and drugs. They also identified dozens of genes expressed differently in younger patients, some associated with metastasis. Kimmie Ng and Ana Anderson, co-senior authors, noted these differences could explain why younger patients face worse outcomes despite healthier profiles. While the study does not prove these traits cause aggressiveness, experts hope the findings will drive research into targeted therapies. Heinz-Josef Lenz cautioned the study lacks proof of causation, but Rachel Issaka emphasized understanding these differences could improve screening and early detection. The research highlights the need for tailored treatments for early-onset colorectal cancer.

item.title: Ritz-Carlton, Laguna Niguel sells for $600 million
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Dana Point landmark Ritz-Carlton, Laguna Niguel resort sells for $600 million
The Ritz-Carlton, Laguna Niguel resort has sold for $600 million to Denver-based private equity firm KSL Capital Partners. The 373-room oceanfront property, located in Dana Point, was valued by hotel analyst Alan Reay at $600 million, citing strong demand for luxury resorts. KSL, which also owns properties like the Westin Hilton Head Island Resort, acquired the resort from Anbang Insurance Group, which purchased it in 2016 for $317.2 million as part of a $5.5 billion deal. The resort recently completed a $50 million renovation and offers events, weddings, and high-end tourism. Peregrine Hospitality, KSL’s management firm, will operate the property. KSL also acquired three luxury properties from Braemar Hotels & Resorts for $437.5 million last summer, including the Ritz-Carlton Sarasota and Hotel Yountville. Reay noted that trophy properties in prime locations remain highly valuable despite market conditions.

item.title: DoorDash CEO: AI agents still far from replacing customer orders
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: DoorDash's CEO: Don't be 'delusional' after just a few hundred AI agent orders
DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said AI agents like Meta's Muse have generated only 'several hundred orders' compared to the company's 3.2 billion global orders in 2025. Customers continue using DoorDash's app and website for orders, with Xu noting users 'come to DoorDash and come back to DoorDash.' He cautioned against overestimating AI agents' current impact, calling it 'delusional' to assume they'll soon replace human-driven ordering. While some users find AI tools helpful for price tracking, many hesitate to let agents make purchases and prefer secure payment methods. DoorDash is testing its own AI tools, including a text-to-order feature and a recipe-based chatbot called Ask DoorDash, which could generate new orders. Xu emphasized balancing innovation with realistic expectations, stating 'you never want to fight gravity' but also avoiding delusion about AI's current role.

item.title: San Diego County to receive up to 1.5 inches of rain by Sunday
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Most of San Diego County expected to get an inch of rain by Sunday afternoon
National Weather Service forecasts 0.70 to 1 inch of rain across most of San Diego County by Sunday afternoon from a subtropical storm that made landfall Saturday evening. Forecasters note higher totals up to 1.5 inches possible in areas from San Diego to Julian due to the storm’s flow pattern. The system, classified as a Pineapple Express, was intensified by El Niño conditions. The annual Susan G. Komen More Than Pink Walk was canceled due to the rain forecast. San Diego is expected to finish October with at least 1.57 inches of precipitation, exceeding the monthly average of 0.50 inches. The storm’s remnants brought significant rainfall to regions typically experiencing drier conditions.

item.title: Ebola outbreak kills over 5,000 in DR Congo's deadliest epidemic
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
More than 5,000 people have died from an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to government data. The outbreak, which began in May, became the country's deadliest in history in August, with 10,300 confirmed cases across eight provinces. The Bundibugyo strain, which has no available treatment or vaccine, is spreading in the conflict-ridden Ituri province. Cases have also been reported in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda. The World Health Organization and UN urge expanded control measures, including community outreach and improved access to affected areas. Previous outbreaks in DR Congo had lower death tolls, but the current one is described as spreading faster. Health workers and a politician have been attacked, including a nurse killed and another injured in an assault linked to accusations of contaminating water sources. Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths early in the outbreak but no new cases since August. Kenya has nine confirmed cases and two deaths, while Nigeria reported two suspected cases. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control says the risk of infection in Europe remains very low.

item.title: SDPD Increases Patrols for Halloween Safety
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: SDPD ramps up presence for Halloween weekend as part of Operation Last Call
San Diego Police Department increased patrols in the Gaslamp Quarter during Halloween weekend as part of Operation Last Call. Despite rainy weather, crowds gathered on Fifth Avenue, with attendees enjoying costumes and festivities. Police deployed additional officers and the Gas and Bike Enforcement Team to manage large crowds and address violent or unlawful behavior. Communications manager Ashley Nicholes stated the department has made 168 arrests and issued 179 citations since the operation began in August. Officers aim to maintain order and ensure public safety. Attendees emphasized the importance of staying together and prioritizing safety. The heightened presence will continue to keep the area safe for residents and visitors.

item.title: San Diego County Offers Halloween-Themed Marriage Ceremonies
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: San Diego County hosts Halloween-themed 'Halloweddings'
San Diego County Assessor-Recorder-County Clerk Jordan Marks is offering Halloween-themed marriage ceremonies Friday. Couples can wed in costume at the downtown office inside the County Administration Center, with staff dressed in holiday attire. Marriage licenses cost $129, and civil ceremonies in English or Spanish cost $107. The event runs until 5 p.m., with free underground parking available. Marks, who also serves as commissioner of civil marriages, invited couples to celebrate their 'enchanted love story' without a 'frightening price tag.' The office issues nearly 25,000 marriage licenses annually and performs over 11,000 weddings, with about half held on-site. The ARCC office also handles birth/death certificates, business registrations, and real estate records. Marks oversees the fifth-largest assessor jurisdiction in the U.S. as a countywide elected official.

item.title: Apollo shares private-equity playbook with nonprofits for operational support
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Apollo is sharing its private-equity playbook with nonprofits
Apollo Asset Management's foundation is sharing its private-equity playbook with 28 nonprofits, offering operational guidance, funding, and strategic support. The initiative, launched in 2022, provides grantees access to Apollo's deal teams of 5-10 employees, who assist with projects, board opportunities, and strategic advice. Over $13 million has been allocated, with a $100 million commitment over a decade. Nonprofits receive funding based on budget size and impact metrics. The foundation also hosts training sessions on AI, leadership, and fundraising, and hosts summits where grantees interact with Apollo executives. Examples include Acceleration Project using Apollo's AI tool to automate client data analysis and The Marcy Lab School revising its curriculum to integrate business and tech skills. Scott Kleinman emphasized the foundation's focus on operational support, not just capital, while Lauren Coape-Arnold highlighted board reorganization for strong governance. Jane Veron noted Apollo helped prioritize 35 process improvements, and Reuben Ogbonna II described curriculum changes based on Apollo's input.

item.title: Boater dies after vessel capsizes near Del Mar jetty
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Boater killed after vessel capsizes near Del Mar jetty
A vessel overturned near the Del Mar Jetty around 7 p.m. Friday, killing one person and injuring another. Lifeguards and the Oceanside Fire Department received a 911 call from a survivor on board. First responders confirmed a missing individual in the water. A search-and-rescue operation located the victim at 7:13 p.m., where the vessel had struck rocks on the jetty. Crews performed CPR on the victim before transporting them to Tri-City Medical Center. Despite efforts, the victim was pronounced dead at the hospital. The surviving individual was also taken to Tri-City Medical Center. Authorities confirmed the incident involved a capsized watercraft near the jetty.

item.title: Ukraine Welcomes Evacuees from Oleshky After Ceasefire
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Ukraine news: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Kyiv-controlled territory
Ukraine welcomed evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky into Kyiv-controlled territory after a localized ceasefire. The town, occupied since 2022, had a pre-invasion population of 24,000, with around 2,000 civilians remaining. Evacuees, including a 1-year-old and a 94-year-old, traveled via Belarus. The U.S. first lady, Melania Trump, was credited with brokering the truce. Ukraine also claimed strikes on a Russian rocket fuel plant in Rostov and military depots in occupied regions. Russian officials demanded peace talks without European involvement, citing existing U.S. contacts. Meanwhile, Russia reported damage from a drone attack near a refinery, though details were unverified. U.S. officials warned of a potential mass casualty plot against a Moscow museum. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy met with Turkish President Erdogan in Istanbul to discuss Black Sea shipping. German Foreign Minister Wadephul stated Europe and the U.S. are 'on the same side' against Russia, emphasizing the necessity of dialogue despite differences.

item.title: John Turturro Guests on 'Wait Wait' Show, October 31, 2026
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Culture Original headline: 'Wait Wait' for October 31, 2026: With Not My Job guest John Turturro
The 'Wait Wait' show for October 31, 2026, was recorded in Chicago with guest host Negin Farsad, judge Alzo Slade, and Not My Job guest John Turturro. Panelists Hari Kondabolu, Paula Poundstone, and Faith Salie participated. The episode featured segments including stories about unexpected companionship, game-changing advice, and a segment titled 'Pickpocket, meet Hot Pocket' where Turturro answered questions about Hot Pockets. Alzo Slade read three limericks about news topics. Panelists also predicted the next surprising romance movie following 'Wicker.' The show included humor and audience interaction, with Turturro discussing his film 'The Only Living Pickpocket in New York.'

item.title: Bolivia declares emergency as El Nino intensifies, threatens severe weather
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle
Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz declared a national state of emergency to address severe droughts and flooding linked to the intensifying El Nino. The decree enables expanded rescue operations and coordination between national, regional authorities, and security forces. Government data shows drought has impacted 78,000 families and caused loss of over 75,000 cattle across seven departments. Floods, flash floods, and landslides are also expected as the rainy season begins. El Nino, a periodic warming of the equatorial Pacific, has strengthened rapidly since June and is projected to become an exceptionally strong event. Researchers estimate it could cause 451,000 excess global deaths from June 2026 to February 2027. The UN warns the El Nino, expected to peak in December, is 'heading off the charts' with long-term impacts. Recent weather patterns linked to El Nino include wildfires in Indonesia and water shortages in India due to weak monsoons.

item.title: AI Enables 'Vibe Manufacturing' for DIY Hardware Creators
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Vibe coding is old news. People are 'vibe manufacturing' now.
AI is enabling 'vibe manufacturing,' allowing individuals to create physical objects without traditional CAD skills. Jeff Deehan used GPT-6 Astra to design a steel camper attachment, which was fabricated by SendCutSend. Amy Zhou and Jake Fitzgerald developed a text-to-CAD tool with over 23,000 GitHub stars, enabling users to generate 3D models for jewelry, robot arms, and brain scans. Zhou's AI-generated charms and Fitzgerald's sheet-metal robot arm demonstrate the approach's versatility. Sourish Sharma used AI to refine a 3D-printed brain model, surpassing open-source tools. While complex projects like cars remain out of reach, simpler items like children's toys and answering machines are feasible. David Plakon built a Tin Can-style answering machine with AI guidance, iterating on designs with his 3D printer. Challenges include design inaccuracies requiring manual adjustments, but AI streamlines prototyping. 'AI literally does replace CAD engineering completely,' Sharma said, noting the shift from coding to hardware creation. The trend highlights AI's role in democratizing manufacturing for hobbyists and small-scale creators.

item.title: Long Beach Closes Coastal Waters After Sewage Main Break
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Massive sewage main break prompts closure of all coastal waters off Long Beach
Ocean waters off Long Beach were closed to swimmers after a sewage main break discharged 29,000 gallons of wastewater near Livingston Drive and 2nd Street. City Health Officer Dr. Cliff Okada ordered the temporary closure of all coastal swimming areas due to potential recreational water quality impacts. The spill, caused by a broken force main, was partially contained with a bypass line and emergency cleanup by Ocean Blue. Of the spill, 15,000 gallons were recovered, and 14,000 gallons were released into the ocean. Repairs are ongoing. State law mandates closures in such cases, and water sampling will resume Monday pending rain. Full beach closures are rare, typically reserved for major emergencies. Nearby areas like Dockweiler State Beach and Santa Monica Pier remained under advisement, while Malibu Point and Avalon Beach saw warnings lifted. The closure underscores concerns over bacterial contamination and water safety standards.
